teodora.style: an old, warm, unhurried market woman, wry and wise

opening.text: Hear ye! The bazaar is open! Five houses, one season, and the Palace is watching.
Cheapest stall in town, and the loudest! Morning, Teodora!
Some of us sell silk, darling. Not noise.
Every rumor is a door. I intend to walk through all of them.
And you, newcomer. Treat the shoppers fairly. They remember.

rumor.text: Caravans outside the gates. Forty camels. Gold on the harnesses.
Gold on a camel? Who is that rich?
Someone who means to buy the bazaar, not trade in it.
Then we shall see whether money can buy taste.

arrival.text: Good people of the bazaar. I am Baltazar, of the Golden Caravan Company.
From today, my prices are the lowest you will ever see. <short pause> I can lose money longer than any of you can stay open.
He is selling below what we pay the caravans! That is not trade, that is war!
Hold on to your customers, child. A man with no friends runs out of patience.

monopoly.text: Prices have changed. <short pause> Mine are the only prices now.
A monopoly is a fortress. Fortresses fall when the well runs dry.

seized.text: A charter, going cheap. I will take it. <short pause> I will take all of them, eventually.
There goes another house. Who is next?

leaves.text: This bazaar is too stubborn to be worth my gold. <sigh> Pack the camels.
Ha! Go back to wherever rich men come from!
Loyal customers, child. Better than any war chest.

wins.text: Five houses, and not one could stand together. <short pause> The bazaar is mine.
By order of the Golden Caravan Company, the bazaar closes early tonight.

end.text: The season is over! The scales are closed and the ledgers sealed.
Count your coins tonight. Tomorrow, the rumors start again.

cry_teodora.text: Tea from the high terraces! Come, children, taste before you buy!
cry_teodora.style: calling out across a busy market, warm and amused, an old trader who knows everyone

cry_teodora.text: Salt as white as an old woman's braids! Fair weight, fair price!
cry_teodora.style: calling out across a busy market, warm and amused, an old trader who knows everyone

cry_teodora.text: Hot tea and honest scales, forty years at this very stall!

cry_kasim.text: Cheapest in the bazaar! Cheaper than cheap! Come, come, come!
cry_kasim.style: shouting at the top of his lungs across a crowded bazaar, fast, cheeky and grinning

cry_kasim.text: Saffron, silk, tea! Kasim beats every price in town, ask anyone!
cry_kasim.style: shouting at the top of his lungs across a crowded bazaar, fast, cheeky and grinning

cry_kasim.text: Why pay more, my friends? Kasim's stall, right here, right now!

cry_vey.text: Silk for those with taste, darling. The rest may keep walking.
cry_vey.style: calling out languidly over the crowd, elegant and amused, never raising her voice too much

cry_vey.text: Silk from the far east, fit for the Palace itself.
cry_vey.style: calling out languidly over the crowd, elegant and amused, never raising her voice too much

cry_vey.text: Touch it, darling. Then tell me it is not worth every coin.

cry_ozzo.text: Saffron, red as a secret, and just as precious.

cry_ozzo.text: The wise buy before the rumor, friends. Ozzo's stall.

bazaar.prompt: A 2-minute instrumental for a cosy trading game set in an old desert-city spice bazaar at golden hour. Oud, qanun, frame drum and darbuka, light hand claps, warm and bustling but calm enough to play under dialogue. About 96 BPM, D Hijaz flavour, steady groove with no big climax, ending in a way that loops smoothly back to the start. Instrumental only, no vocals.

magnate.prompt: A 90-second instrumental for a trading game when a ruthless rich tycoon arrives to crush the local merchants. Low strings, deep tombak and dohol pulses, ticking riq, a menacing ney melody, rising tension that stays under dialogue, about 84 BPM, minor key, loops smoothly. Instrumental only, no vocals.

finale.prompt: A 45-second instrumental finale for the end of a season in a desert bazaar trading game: triumphant oud and strings with frame drums, warm brass swell, ending on a resolved final chord. Instrumental only, no vocals.
